name: createContext()
description: Creates a Context object that components can provide a value to and read from, without passing that value explicitly through every level of props.
parameters: defaultValue — the value used by consumers when no matching Provider is found above them in the tree.
returns: A Context object with .Provider and .Consumer components.
notes: The default value is only used when a component reads the context without any Provider above it — it does not act as a global fallback once a Provider exists.

name: Context.Provider
description: The component that supplies a context's value to all descendant components, overriding the default value for that subtree.
parameters: value — the current value to make available to consuming components.
notes: Every descendant that reads this context re-renders whenever `value` changes (by reference), regardless of how deeply nested it is.

name: Context.Consumer
description: A component that subscribes to a context using a render-prop function, for reading context inside class components or where useContext isn't available.
notes: In function components, useContext() is simpler and preferred; Consumer is mainly needed in class components.

name: Context vs Prop Drilling
description: Context is best reserved for genuinely global or widely-shared data (theme, auth user, locale); for data used by only a couple of nearby components, passing props is usually simpler and easier to trace.
notes: Overusing Context for everything can make data flow harder to follow than straightforward prop passing.

name: Context Performance Considerations
description: Every component consuming a context re-renders whenever the Provider's value reference changes, even if the component only cares about part of that value — so unmemoized objects passed as value cause frequent re-renders.
notes: Splitting frequently- and rarely-changing data into separate contexts, or memoizing the value, reduces unnecessary re-renders.

name: Combining Multiple Contexts
description: Nesting several Provider components to make multiple independent pieces of context data available at once, keeping each concern in its own context.
notes: Wrapping the nested providers in a single 'AppProviders' component keeps the app's root tree readable as the number of contexts grows.
